lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs are finally playing like a team that remembers how quickly a season can tilt. Tuesday's 6-2 demolition of Columbus made it two victories in two nights of work, with Kirill Marchenko scoring in his return to Nationwide Arena and Easton Cowan delivering a goal and two assists. Cowan's short-handed marker was particularly telling - the young forward is no longer merely auditioning for responsibility. Auston Matthews added a goal and an assist in his 700th NHL game, while Anthony Stolarz stopped 33 shots. The blemish was Jake McCabe, who left after taking a high stick near his left eye and did not return; Chris Tanev's absence already makes that blue line a precarious place. At 5-4, Toronto sits fifth in the Eastern Conference with 12 points, three behind the lead. Thursday's 7 p.m. meeting with the Rangers is the next test: prove this two-game streak is a turn, not a twitch.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's offseason has already supplied its first useful argument: sentiment won't rebuild this roster. The Blue Jays finished 79-83, second in the AL East, but the address is now 2027. Shane Bieber's possible return has become the early headline, with Ben Nicholson-Smith identifying pitching targets and reopening the door to a reunion. Bieber is an intriguing piece, not a complete repair job; Toronto needs rotation depth sturdy enough to survive the injuries that exposed the roster's thin spots. The encouraging note comes from Arizona, where prospect Joe Bloss struck out six over 2⅔ innings for Mesa - a reminder that help may be developing, though not fast enough to excuse inaction. This club needs more than a familiar name and a hopeful spring. Watch whether Ross Atkins adds established starting pitching before camp, and whether Bloss can force his way into the 2027 conversation.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors' preseason ended with a thud, but the real drama arrives tonight, when nostalgia meets a roster still being assembled. Kawhi Leonard's tribute video ahead of his Toronto return has turned the regular-season opener into a civic event, though sentiment will not set a screen or defend the point of attack. Toronto is 0-0 and officially second in the Atlantic, 0.5 games behind - preseason exhibitions do not count, even after Friday's 129-125 loss to Detroit. The practical work continues: Toronto exercised options on Collin Murray-Boyles and Ja'Kobe Walter, securing two young pieces through 2027-28, while rookie Allen Graves faces a crowded rotation and may accept a Raptors 905 assignment. Nate Bittle is out with an avulsion injury. Now watch the 7:30 p.m. meeting with Chicago: lineup choices, Leonard's integration and whether this young team can turn reunion energy into a credible opening statement.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders are not merely losing games; they are losing the margin for error that keeps a season alive. Terry McLaurin's season-ending torn patellar tendon is the cruelest blow yet, arriving one day after Washington's 23-17 loss to San Francisco and removing Jayden Daniels' most trusted target. At 1-4-1, Washington sits fourth in the NFC East, two games behind, with a one-game losing streak and an offense now forced to find answers quickly. Daniels remains the central figure - the quarterback's talent is evident, but the 49ers exposed how much sharper his decisions and the surrounding operation must become in critical moments. This is a team short on victories and now short on its best receiver. The next test is the Week 8 prime-time meeting with Philadelphia, where Washington must show whether it can replace McLaurin by committee - and stop turning winnable moments into another lost Sunday.

article.title: Leafs Beat Blue Jackets Behind Cowan
paragraphs: The Leafs beat the Blue Jackets 6-2 in Columbus on Tuesday, with Nick Robertson scoring twice and Matthew Knies adding three points. Anthony Stolarz stopped 35 shots for a .946 save percentage, while the Leafs moved to 5-4 and fifth in the Eastern Conference. Toronto hosts the Rangers Thursday at 7:00 PM ET on TSN.

The Jays are looking ahead to Arizona Fall League action, where fans can watch Toronto prospects. The Raptors open their preseason schedule against the Bulls tonight at 7:30 PM ET, with Bittle out because of a foot injury. The Commanders next play the Eagles on Sunday, November 1, and wide receiver Terry McLaurin is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon.
